# Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence

# Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-09 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] Rootly’s Acknowledge, Snooze, and Escalate Alerts changelog describes an optional retrigger-acknowledged-alert setting: after ACK, a snooze timeout re-pages the same responder about an open alert. This is an unresolved-work reminder mechanism, distinct from escalation caused by a missing ACK. (low confidence) — https://rootly.com/changelog/acknowledge-snooze-and-escalate-alerts
- [statement] Grafana IRM’s response documentation warns that a new alert joining an acknowledged alert group does not trigger escalation-chain actions. Group-level acknowledgement therefore needs to be considered when checking whether a later alert obtained a fresh responder response. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/
- [statement] PagerDuty advances to the next escalation rule when nobody acts before its escalation timeout. Grafana Cloud IRM similarly escalates an alert that is not acknowledged or resolved within its configured timeframe. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/
- [statement] An escalation chain is not a guarantee of eventual human response: Grafana Cloud IRM stops when all steps complete, and PagerDuty stops notifying after configured repeats and the final responder contact methods are exhausted. A bot monitor should test and expose this exhausted-chain outcome. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/escalation-and-routing/escalation-chains/ · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PagerDuty documents a terminal escalation failure mode: when configured policy loops are exhausted, the incident remains assigned to the last user and stops notifying after cycling through that responder’s contact methods. Repeated notification is therefore bounded by policy configuration. (low confidence) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Google SRE describes paging response times as an agreement between the team and business system owners. Its primary/secondary rotations can use the secondary as a fall-through for pages the primary misses; these are organizational patterns rather than a universal crypto-bot deadline. (low confidence) — https://sre.google/sre-book/being-on-call/
- [statement] PagerDuty snapshots the service escalation policy when an incident triggers and uses that version through its lifecycle; reassigning to the same updated policy records a new snapshot. Incident evidence should identify the policy effective for the incident rather than assume the current policy was used. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies

## Facts and statements

- [statement] In PagerDuty and Grafana Cloud IRM, acknowledgement indicates that a responder is investigating or working on an issue and stops automatic escalation notifications; it is distinct from resolution. A crypto bot monitor integrating these tools should therefore keep acknowledgement and resolution as separate states. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/
- [statement] Missing-ACK escalation depends on configured timeouts and fallback targets. PagerDuty advances through ordered rules if nobody acts before the timeout; the cited vendor’s routing article warns that a single schedule tier without fallback tiers can leave an alert unacknowledged. (medium confidence) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://incident.io/blog/intelligent-alert-routing-vs-escalation
- [statement] For response evidence, separate responder actions from message delivery: Grafana IRM exposes acknowledged/resolved times and records who manually advanced escalation; the PagerDuty case study in Google’s incident-response workbook uses a scribe ledger of actions, owners, and timestamps. These are concrete inputs for an auditable handoff record. (medium confidence) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/ · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/
- [statement] PagerDuty’s Prometheus integration guide says automatic resolution depends on `send_resolved` not being `false`; resolve notifications may wait until the next `group_interval`, and delivery is described as best effort. A source-side recovery signal does not establish immediate downstream incident resolution. (low confidence) — https://www.pagerduty.com/docs/guides/prometheus-integration-guide/
- [statement] Grafana OnCall issue 3161 records a historical ACK/resolve race: the reporter expected a near-simultaneous resolve to take priority, while a contributor explained that acknowledging a resolved group intentionally transitions it through unresolved to acknowledged. This is an attributed historical behavior, not proof about current Grafana IRM. (low confidence) — https://github.com/grafana-cold-storage/oncall/issues/3161
- [statement] A reporter in Grafana OnCall issue 4760 described direct paging continuing according to personal notification policies after the user acknowledged the group, on Docker version v1.8.8. Treat this as a historical bug report to motivate verification, not a confirmed defect in the current product. (low confidence) — https://github.com/grafana-cold-storage/oncall/issues/4760
- [statement] GoAlert v0.35.0 release notes document opt-in multi-ack escalation steps: each activated user continues receiving notifications until acknowledging individually, while escalation to the next step stops after the first ACK and closing cancels pending notifications. The alert log records each user’s ACK. (low confidence) — https://github.com/target/goalert/releases
- [statement] In the July 2026 GoAlert issue 4531, the author reported that derived on-call ownership did not provide per-alert handoff or a reliable list of a responder’s own alerts, and proposed explicit assignment. This is a user-reported design gap and proposal, not evidence that the proposed assignment behavior shipped. (low confidence) — https://github.com/target/goalert/issues/4531
- [statement] The cited vendor changelog dated March 17, 2026 announces escalation-acked entries in the incident timeline. This supplies product-specific acknowledgement evidence but does not by itself establish that operational recovery occurred. (low confidence) — https://incident.io/changelog/post-mortems-upgrade
- [statement] PagerDuty distinguishes the escalation timeout for an unanswered incident from the acknowledgement timeout for an already acknowledged incident. Reaching the latter returns the incident to triggered status and resumes escalation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/incidents
- [statement] Both PagerDuty and Grafana Cloud IRM skip escalation schedule steps with no on-call responder and proceed onward; the existence of a configured schedule alone does not establish coverage. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/escalation-policies · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/escalation-and-routing/escalation-chains/
- [statement] PagerDuty incident timelines expose timestamps for incident statuses, actions and sent notifications. Grafana Cloud IRM exposes acknowledgement and resolution dates, assigned responders and escalation-chain progress. These are concrete evidence surfaces for reconstructing a bot-alert response. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/incidents · keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence · also: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/
- [statement] Grafana Cloud IRM can manually advance an unfinished escalation chain. The timeline records who advanced it with an `escalation manually advanced` entry; advancing an acknowledged or silenced group clears that state and resumes escalation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/respond-to-alerts/
- [statement] Grafana Cloud IRM recommends testing escalation chains with non-production alerts before use; this supplies a direct basis for a bot monitor drill that verifies paging, acknowledgement and fallback behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/respond-to-incidents/escalation-and-routing/escalation-chains/
